entries.test: Public prompt-and-output studies showing how reliably DALL-E 2 follows complex sentences and relational words such as “similar” would test this claim.
entries.note: The surrounding examples give “easily fooled” a concrete reading as failures to follow the requested relationships.

entries.test: The original Gemini example and Marcus's Microsoft Designer interaction record would show whether he reproduced the same failure on his first attempt.
entries.note: The supplied text does not show what “this” refers to; identifying it specifically as a compositional failure requires the omitted example.

entries.test: The prompt, generated images, and interaction history from Marcus's reported first attempt would show whether any horse was riding an astronaut.
entries.note: This concerns the reported attempt with a bowl of cherries added, not all image models or attempts.

entries.test: Controlled public tests of DALL-E 2 using equivalent canonical and noncanonical prompts would show whether prompt interpretation accounts for the horse-riding-astronaut failure despite demonstrated drawing capability.
entries.note: The causal claim concerns the discussed failure, not every limitation of DALL-E.

entries.test: Public experiments holding the requested scene constant while changing its linguistic formulation would test whether DALL-E's failure arises from language interpretation despite its ability to render the scene.
entries.note: The language-understanding claim has a behavioral test; it does not require treating the model as having private human beliefs.
“Anything is possible” is an ironic setup immediately undercut by “Oh, no wait. That didn’t work.” The normalization turns it into a general factual claim.

entries.test: The three outputs in the final reported Gemini attempt would show whether exactly one correctly depicted a horse riding an astronaut.
entries.note: The denominator refers to the final set of outputs, not all attempts across the session.

entries.test: Public Gemini interaction records and repeated trials with the requested scene would show successful generation alongside the frequency of failures and retries required.
entries.note: “Like pulling teeth” describes difficulty grounded in the reported repeated failures and eventual success.

entries.test: Comparable public evaluations of generative models available in May 2022 and February 2024 would show whether factual accuracy and compositional performance improved.
entries.note: The surrounding retrospective supplies the 2022 baseline. This is a firm claim of no progress, even though no particular benchmark is named.
